intentComment: Story 003 (local-deploy) + Story 073. `dev` is the one-command local development orchestration: wipe local state, start anvil, cold-deploy the ENTIRE Phoenix Phase-2 system against mocked mainnet dependencies, simulate a DOLA yield tick, extract the address book, regenerate the TypeScript address interface, and serve it over HTTP on :3001 for the Phoenix UI. Story 073 extended the local deploy to mirror the mainnet NudgeStreamer cutover planned in story 072 (streamer-buffered nudge donations, BatchNFTMinterMultiToken with USDC/phUSD/Kendu, NudgeRatchet back at index 7) and added a V1->NFTStakerMigrator->NFTStakerDepletionV2 migration REHEARSAL so story 072's riskiest mainnet phase can be dry-run for free.

base.command: npm run clean:local && npm run start:anvil & sleep 3 && npm run deploy:local && ./simulate-yield.sh && npm run extract:addresses && npm run generate:ts-anvil && npm run serve
base.shellSemantics: The single `&` is a BACKGROUNDING operator, not `&&`. Bash parses this as TWO jobs: job A = `npm run clean:local && npm run start:anvil` (backgrounded), job B = `sleep 3 && npm run deploy:local && ... && npm run serve` (foreground). Consequences: (1) anvil runs detached in the background and is never killed by this script — unlike `test:nft-flow`, which ends with `kill %1`; (2) readiness is a fixed 3-second sleep, not a health probe, so a slow machine races the deploy against anvil startup; (3) `clean:local` executes inside the backgrounded job while the foreground job's `sleep 3` runs concurrently — but `deploy:local` re-runs `clean:local` itself, so the wipe is idempotent and the race is benign.

noPreviewVariantNote: There is no `dev:preview` / `dev:dry`. Unlike the mainnet entry points in this repo (which all carry a PREVIEW_MODE=true sibling), DeployMocks has no PREVIEW_MODE branch at all — the only way to run it is to broadcast against a throwaway local chain. Re-running the audit's execution step therefore means re-running the whole `dev` chain against a fresh anvil in workspace/, not a read-only preview.

steps.runsIn: backgrounded job A, and AGAIN inside deploy:local (step 3)
deletes: broadcast/*/31337  (all anvil-chain forge broadcast run records; mainnet broadcast/*/1 untouched)
steps.staleWindow: addresses.ts / local-addresses.ts survive the wipe. If the chain aborts after clean:local but before generate:ts-anvil (e.g. deploy failure, or simulate-yield.sh's `set -e` firing on a missing progress file / null jq lookup), the repo is left with COMMITTED TypeScript address files pointing at a chain that no longer exists, with nothing but an ISO comment distinguishing them from fresh output.

steps.runsIn: backgrounded job A; never killed by this entry point
steps.note: --host 0.0.0.0 binds on every interface, not just loopback. --block-time 2 means blocks mine every 2s, which is what makes `--slow` broadcast wall-clock-expensive and is why the migration rehearsal's committedDebt accrues between simulate and replay (see closure-manifest divergence D-14).

steps.command: npm run clean:local && forge script script/DeployMocks.s.sol:DeployMocks --rpc-url http://localhost:8545 --broadcast --slow --gas-estimate-multiplier 300
steps.onChainEffect: Cold deploy of ~70 contracts + ~120 configuration calls against anvil. See closure-manifest.json -> deployedContracts.

flags.--broadcast: signs and sends; no dry-run mode exists
flags.--slow: one tx at a time, awaiting confirmation — required because Router02 deadline and the migration rehearsal are timestamp-sensitive
flags.--gas-estimate-multiplier 300: 3x gas estimates; blunt workaround for estimation misses on this very large script

steps.resumeMechanism: NONE. DeployMocks never reads a progress file (no vm.readFile / parseJson anywhere in the file); clean:local deletes it first; it is cold-deploy-only. The checkpoint/resume pattern described in the project CLAUDE.md exists only in the mainnet scripts.
steps.progressFileShape: Hand-assembled by string.concat in _writeProgressFile() (:1918-1945) — no vm.writeJson/vm.serializeJson, no escaping. deploymentStatus is the HARD-CODED literal "completed" (:1922), not derived from anything; the file always claims success if execution reaches the end. Emitted after vm.stopBroadcast(), i.e. during forge's local execution phase.

steps.onChainEffect: cast send MockDola.mint(MockAutoDOLA, 2300e18) — mints 2300 DOLA DIRECTLY TO the ERC4626 vault without minting shares, so totalAssets rises while totalSupply does not. That is the whole simulation: a one-shot donation-style share-price bump for MockAutoDOLA, giving ERC4626YieldStrategy(DOLA) claimable yield for StableYieldAccumulator to gather.
steps.whatItDoesNotSimulate: Only the DOLA vault. MockAutoUSDC, MockSUSDS, MockSUSDe get NO yield tick from this script (DeployMocks already seeds 1000 DOLA + 1000 USDC one-off at Phase 9.5/9.6). There is no time-based accrual, no repeated ticks, and no yield for the USDe market strategy, so the AMM-slippage path is never exercised under accrual.
steps.credentials: Hard-codes anvil default key 0xac09...ff80 and RPC http://localhost:8545. Not parameterized.
steps.failureMode: `set -e` + explicit guards: exits 1 if progress.31337.json is missing or either jq lookup is null. Requires jq, bc, cast on PATH.

reads: server/deployments/progress.31337.json (path built from __dirname, CWD-independent; exit 1 if missing)
steps.outputShape: { chainId, networkName, deploymentStatus (all copied verbatim from progress), extractedAt (ISO now), contracts: { <displayName>: { address, deployed, configured, deployGas, configGas } } } — flat map, no ABIs.
transforms: 1. drop entries whose address == 0x0 (the checkpoint markers Seeding / UsdcSeeding / DolaYield / UsdcYield)

2. MOCK-PREFIX STRIP: name.startsWith('Mock') ? name.slice(4) : name — a blind 4-char slice. MockPhUSD -> PhUSD, MockAutoDOLA -> AutoDOLA, MockKendu -> Kendu. THIS IS THE MECHANISM BY WHICH A MOCK BECOMES INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE REAL THING DOWNSTREAM.
4. drop UNISWAP_V2_BACKING_NAMES = [WETH9, UniswapV2Factory, UniswapV2Router02, UniPool{EYE,SCX,FLX}, UniRoutePool{WETH,USDS,DOLA}]
5. drop bare V1 NFT names [NFTMinter, BurnerEYE, BurnerSCX, BurnerFlax, BalancerPooler, GatherWBTC]
6. V2->base rename: NFTMinterV2 -> NFTMinter, BalancerPoolerV2 -> BalancerPooler, GatherWBTCV2 -> GatherWBTC
steps.liveButUnusedAffordance: CHAIN_OUTPUT_MAP still maps 1 -> mainnet.json, so `node server/extract-addresses.js 1` succeeds and writes an orphaned server/deployments/mainnet.json from the stale, step-marker-polluted progress.1.json. No npm script invokes it and nothing reads the output, but the affordance is live and its output would look authoritative.

reads: server/deployments/local.json (exit 1 with "Run 'npm run extract:addresses' first." if absent)
writes: server/deployments/addresses.ts  — `export interface ContractAddresses { <Name>: string; ... }`, one member per local.json contracts key, insertion order, plus a generated-on header comment

server/deployments/local-addresses.ts — `import { ContractAddresses } from './addresses'; export const anvilAddresses: ContractAddresses = {...}; export type AnvilContractName = keyof ContractAddresses;`
steps.anvilOnly: chainId 1 hits an explicit `REFUSING:` branch + process.exit(1). The mainnet codegen path was deliberately removed (story 068); mainnet-addresses.ts is hand-maintained and patched by scripts/patch-mainnet-addresses-*.js.
steps.couplingHazard: The ContractAddresses INTERFACE is regenerated from ANVIL data, but server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts is annotated `: ContractAddresses`. A purely local deploy change therefore breaks the mainnet address file's type-check until zero-address placeholders are hand-added — which is exactly what story-073 commit d241e61 did for Kendu and NudgeStreamer. Contract names are emitted raw with no TS-identifier sanitization.
steps.orphanedFile: server/deployments/mainnet-essential-addresses.json documents itself as "the durable preservation source merged into mainnet-addresses.ts on every chainId-1 codegen run" — but that codegen path now hard-refuses chainId 1 and a repo-wide grep finds ZERO consumers. The comment is false; external mainnet addresses survive only because the hand-maintained file is edited surgically.

steps.listen: process.env.API_PORT || 3001 on API_HOST || localhost; express + cors() with NO origin allowlist
endpoints: GET /            — static doc blob with a hand-written, now-stale availableContracts list of 18 names (actual = 57)
GET /contracts   — flat { name: address } derived from local.json
GET /contracts/:contractName — { name, address, deployed, configured }; 404 body lists all available names
steps.hardCoded31337: Both loaders are hard-wired to 31337; there is no multi-network support despite the CLAUDE.md spec, and the response shape does not match the documented {networks:{...}, activeNetwork, availableNetworks} contract. No ABIs are served.

notInThisChain.generate:hooks: `wagmi generate` -> hooks/generated.ts is NOT part of `dev`. It is run manually via `npm run generate:hooks` / `npm run update:hooks` (generate + version patch + publish to npm.pkg.github.com as @behodler/phase2-wagmi-hooks). wagmi.config.ts has contracts: [] and a single foundry({project:'.', include:[~40 artifact names]}) plugin with NO `deployments:` block — so generated.ts carries ABIs only and embeds zero addresses (grep -c 0x == 0). It reads out/ artifacts, so it depends on a prior `forge build` and on foundry.toml's skip list.

forgeTarget.chainGuard: NONE — no require(block.chainid == 31337) anywhere in the file, despite the project CLAUDE.md mandating that anvil relaxations be gated behind an explicit `block.chainid == 31337` branch. The only 31337 coupling is the hard-coded output path in _writeProgressFile.

operationalObservations: No chainid guard in DeployMocks — the project's own CLAUDE.md requires anvil relaxations to sit behind an explicit `block.chainid == 31337` branch. Every unrestricted-mint mock, every `phUSD.setMinter(deployer, true)`, and the whole migration rehearsal are un-gated code paths.

`deploymentStatus: "completed"` is a hard-coded string literal written after local execution, before/independent of broadcast confirmation. Benign on anvil (no resume consumer) but it is the same write-before-broadcast shape that already poisoned three committed progress.uniboost-cutover.1.POISONED*.bak files on mainnet.

Everything in server/deployments/ is committed to git, including the regenerated local.json / progress.31337.json / addresses.ts / local-addresses.ts. Every local `dev` run dirties the tree, and a local-only mock addition propagates into the tracked ContractAddresses interface that the MAINNET address book must satisfy.
anvil is backgrounded and never killed by `dev` (contrast `test:nft-flow`, which ends with `kill %1`). Repeated `dev` invocations will fail on a port-8545 bind unless anvil is killed manually.
